title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Mission Control. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Mission Control
options.lineage: Apollo Mission Operations Control Room, Houston, 1965–72
options.thesis: Your career run as a live mission: the cosmos on the front wall, you at the flight director's console.
options.viewport: The front wall is one giant projection screen playing real NASA footage; beneath it a console strip carries your callsign, role and a lit OPEN TO WORK event light.
options.risk: Slides into the sci-fi HUD cliché if drawn as neon glass instead of 1969 hardware.

raised.raise: Motion is real physics, not tweens: orbit traces and the galaxy loop are simulated, the way floated pigment can only move as liquid moves.
Console rows stack in courses whose measure matches their content, so the record reads in the order it was built.
Colour lives only in lit legends and the wall feed; every text field stays achromatic.

options.label: Webb Release Plates
options.thesis: Every project published like a Webb image release: the plate full-bleed, compass and scale bar, filters as the stack.
options.viewport: A full-bleed Webb plate with your name set as the release title, a filter legend where the subtitle would sit, and a compass rose pointing at the work.
options.risk: Also where most space portfolios land: real telescope imagery is this category's strongest cliché when composed timidly.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.lineage: film editor's select rail and trim bin
options.thesis: The work as a strung reel: each project a punched frame on a perforated rail, cosmos footage in the windows.
options.viewport: A grain-orange field crossed by one perforated rail; the first frame plays the cosmos, your name on the slate.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and holds clarity (eight projects become eight frames); loses on audience identification to a space-engineering world.
options.risk: Reads as a film-studio site if the frames stop carrying space footage.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.lineage: printed celestial atlases, red-flashlight observing charts
options.thesis: The portfolio as a chart plate: projects plotted as stars sized by weight, an index pointing into each.
options.viewport: A canvas star chart filling the screen, your work plotted as the brightest stars, name set as the chart title.
options.case: Holds audience identification strongly, but it is the nearest neighbour to the world you just retired.
options.risk: Feels like the old Observation Log in new clothes.

options.label: High-Density Index
options.thesis: Everything a recruiter needs on one packed screen: ruled modules, red tabs, cosmos imagery in every box.
options.viewport: A dense mosaic of ruled modules; the lead module plays the galaxy simulation, name and status in a red-tabbed header.
options.case: Wins on skim clarity, loses on audience identification and on your cosmos-first answer.
options.risk: Buries the cinematic cosmos moment you asked to lead with.

options.label: Floated Pigment
options.thesis: Colour floated and combed into figures, every mark made by moving liquid.
options.viewport: A fluid canvas the visitor combs through.
options.case: Fuses poorly: beautiful, but a recruiter cannot find the facts in liquid.
options.kept: Motion as real physics, not tweened decoration.

options.label: Coiled Earth Tower
options.thesis: A slow ascending record of courses.
options.viewport: A rising tower of text courses.
options.case: Fuses poorly: earth and clay say nothing about space or engineering.
options.kept: Rows whose measure matches their content, stacked in build order.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.thesis: Colour confined to a hairline spectral fringe.
options.viewport: A white field with one iridescent edge.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a white daylight world against a cosmos brief.
options.kept: Colour only where it carries meaning; text fields stay achromatic.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark cinematic space portfolio, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Full-bleed nebula video, your name large over it, a project grid one scroll down.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other space portfolio by design.
